chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from al-Hajjal from Tha'laba from Ma'mar ibn Yahya said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbid the ghusl when one enters the grave.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing ghusl when entering the grave?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi records Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) prohibiting the ritual bath (ghusl) for the person who enters the grave to place the deceased inside. This ruling highlights the distinction between the impurity of the grave itself and the state of the person entering it, a point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding whether the grave is a place of minor or major impurity. It underscores the practical application of purity laws in funeral rites, emphasizing that entering the grave does not automatically necessitate a full ritual bath unless other conditions of impurity are met.
